decision_rule.ADMITTED: ALL FOUR hold: (1) the CI95 LOWER bound of the paired official pooled SLU-F1 delta (B8b minus B7r) is greater than 0; (2) intent is NON-INFERIOR at the own-null margin -- its CI95 lower bound exceeds -1.0051 pp; (3) the TRAIN symmetric scorer slurp-slu-f1-normalized-v1-train AGREES IN SIGN with the unprojected primary; and (4) NO scenario loses intent beyond the null band -- no scenario's paired intent CI95 UPPER bound lies below zero.
decision_rule.HARMFUL: owner decision 25's Method B form, and it is read FIRST: a MEASURED LOSS -- a point estimate of official pooled SLU or of intent below -h (-1.1218 / -1.0051), or a CI95 UPPER bound below zero. An interval that straddles zero with the point estimate inside the margin is NOT harmful.
decision_rule.NEUTRAL: otherwise -- not a measured loss and not all four ADMITTED clauses. Where an interval straddles zero the verdict states 'non-inferiority not proven' in those words.
decision_rule.comparator: cell B7r's sealed score artifact, and nothing else, for every gating clause
decision_rule.harmful_consequence: a HARMFUL cell enters no default plan and its successor in the queue does not fly on its base (owner decision 15)
decision_rule.neutral_and_the_default_plan: design section 15 resolution 5 fixes that a NEUTRAL node-context cell enters the SLURP default plan ONLY IF IT LOWERS COST. A NEUTRAL B8b DOES NOT enter the default plan: the block adds a measured 62-231 words of context on every Reviewer contact that receives a parseable draft and removes nothing, so it lowers no cost. An ADMITTED B8b enters the plan on its measured gain, as any admitted module does.

failure_policy: Stop and preserve on the first failure. No automatic restart, replay, row filtering, roster, role-graph, prompt, geometry or cap change, and no silent recovery. AT MOST ONE root-diagnosed recovery re-registration per flight; a second failure closes that flight and the fix must be proven on a four-row dry run before the block is proposed again. A failed four-row smoke stops cell B8b until the fix is proven on that same four-row roster. One experiment in flight at a time. RESUME-RECOVERY CLAUSE (owner decision 22 of 2026-09-18): if an attempt dies of an INFRASTRUCTURE failure with code and request bytes unchanged -- never a harness or config defect -- the one allowed recovery may be a RESUME-RECOVERY under item E10 instead of a re-fly: every complete row of the aborted attempt is kept without selection, every partial or unstarted row is flown under the same run id, and the merged manifest declares the predecessor attempt with its trace hash, kept-row list and that list's hash. It changes no question, roster, factor, comparator, decision rule or cap, and the run-cumulative budget must be re-checked because a resumed attempt and its predecessor share one run id.

second_declared_key_not_a_factor.the_asymmetry_it_creates_and_how_it_is_r: It CAN change an outcome, on exactly the rows where a completion hits the cap. Cell B7r's comparator arm will have been flown under the base's own policy, so a SEALED B7r arm implies B7r met no finite completion at all -- had it met one, it would have aborted rather than sealed. Any B8b row whose terminal_disposition.reason is 'finite_completion' is therefore a row the comparator could not have produced, and the pair is not clean on that row. The count of such rows is a MANDATORY diagnostic (see diagnostics_required); if it is zero, the contrast is unaffected and the verdict says so; if it is non-zero, the verdict reports the count, the rows and the primary metric recomputed with those rows excluded, BESIDE the registered all-rows number, which stays the number the decision rule reads. NO ROW IS EVER FILTERED OUT of the scored manifest -- every retained row is scored as delivered.

The capped completion itself is quarantined and never becomes the delivered answer: rails.runner refuses the episode unless the disposition's rejected_contact matches the actual quarantined completion hash for hash.

criteria: 1. CONTACTS. The trace carries Perception, Solver, Reviewer and Planner contacts -- about five per row plus any revision the Planner issues (the sealed anchor realized 5.016 per row at this geometry) -- and NO row exceeds the program ceiling of 11.

2. THE RECEIPT ON EVERY REVIEWER CONTACT OF 4 OF 4 ROWS. Each Reviewer contact's reviewer:current-draft row of the saea-node-context-policy-v1 receipt carries a slot_audit block with schema saea-reviewer-slot-audit-v1, view_id slot-audit-v1, release_sha256 eaa2dd0db4d089f9bf1687d353f129ffcf062766f84150b0b93463617fdee7f9, snapshot_sha256 0cc3f96c98addad37fb564483f051dbe1a11145ac554a85918312c388573406c, table_content_hash d4cd4bf3fd9bf44725f860257800c415164faf14a8dcce19bd3ab2339fee01de, template_id probes/ncp_slurp_slot_audit_reviewer_v1.txt, template_sha256 88cc927d901a45ac2496f92453521184cb5b8d39cbf98aa881872b9116d24d0a, the three declared thresholds, and flag_counts carrying all four flag names including the zeros. A contact whose draft did not parse carries applied false with reason draft-unparsed and no block, which is acceptable on that contact; but at least one Reviewer contact of EVERY row must carry applied true, or the smoke has not shown the block reaching the model.

3. THE BLOCK IS AN ADDITION AND REACHES NOTHING ELSE. On every Reviewer contact that rendered a block, the last block_chars characters of the rendered reviewer:current-draft text hash to block_sha256, and the text before them (minus the one joining newline) is the boundary's own L1 rendering. NO other boundary row carries a slot_audit block and every other boundary row keeps its pre-E12 fields. The compilation record's template_sha256s carries the three assets the block was composed from.

4. THE NON-REVIEWER CHANNEL IS CELL B7r's. The Perception request of each of the four rows is BYTE-IDENTICAL to cell B7r's own sealed four-row smoke (run SAEA-SLURP-NATIVE-NCP-L1-REVIEWER-FORMAT-ANCHOR-SMOKE-4-V1) on 4 of 4 rows -- it precedes every generation, so nothing else can explain a difference -- and the Solver and Planner requests are byte-identical wherever their upstream model responses are. Greedy decoding at temperature 0 is not bitwise reproducible across batch compositions and the Reviewer's own text legitimately changes, so a differing Solver or Planner request whose upstream responses differ is NOT a failure; a differing Perception request IS.

5. FIT AND SEAL. One *.request-fit.json per realized contact under the FIT attempt directory, every one with every_request_fits true and every required-token count below 24,576; the worker prints a seal; the manifest seals clean; the tree is still clean.

6. THE FINITE PATH IS REPORTED, NOT REQUIRED. Any row whose terminal_disposition.reason is 'finite_completion' is RETAINED, not an error, and the smoke report states the count and which rows. Four rows are very unlikely to hit the 512-token cap, so the expected count is zero; a non-zero count is acceptable and is itself useful evidence that the retained path works in flight. What is NOT acceptable is an abort on finish_reason 'length': that would mean the declared policy did not reach the runtime.
smoke_acceptance.expected_but_not_required: On the released table the block is 372-992 characters for a draft carrying at most one entity type (62-170 words), so most Reviewer contacts will carry a few hundred characters and zero to three flags. WHICH flags fire on these four rows is neither predicted nor required: the flag logic is proved by tests/unit/test_slurp_slot_audit_view.py and tests/unit/test_reviewer_slot_audit_block.py over the real table, not by four rows. A row on which no flag fires is equally acceptable provided criteria 1-5 hold.
smoke_acceptance.never: no scorer, no answer, reference or quality interpretation, and no task-quality claim. A structural smoke result is never a quality result.

the_analysis_and_its_boundary.fillers_never_rendered: the draft's fillers are read only by the REPRESENTATION predicate and never reach a rendered line; a flag names a TYPE and its counts

flags.EMPTY-DRAFT: the draft declares no entity while at least empty_draft_min_entity_row_share (0.5) of this intent's construction rows carry one
flags.MISSING-COMMON: a type above missing_common_min_row_share (0.5) of this intent's construction rows is absent from the draft; date and time are named like any other type
flags.REPRESENTATION: a date or time filler breaks the released spoken-form convention saea-spoken-form-v1 -- no ASCII digit, no colon, no slash
flags.TYPE-UNSEEN: a draft entity type is not attested with this intent anywhere in the construction pool

the_analysis_and_its_boundary.thresholds_note: profile_min_row_share (0.05) bounds how many types the profile LISTS and gates no flag. All four flags are computed by the HARNESS (rails.slot_audit.slot_audit_flags), never by a model.
